cues.en: If we look around us,
much of what surrounds us

cues.zh: 最初都是各种岩石和污泥，
cues.en: started life as various rocks and sludge
buried in the ground in various places in the world.

cues.zh: 当然，它们现在看起来不像岩石和污泥了。
cues.en: But, of course, they don't look like rocks and sludge now.

cues.zh: 它们看起来像电视摄像机、监视器、
cues.en: They look like TV cameras, monitors,
annoying radio mics.
And so this magical transformation

cues.zh: 正是我想通过我的项目去探究的，
cues.en: is what I was trying to get at with my project,

cues.zh: 这个项目后来被称为烤面包机计划。
cues.en: which became known as the Toaster Project.

cues.zh: 它也受到这句话的启发，
cues.en: And it was also inspired by this quote
from Douglas Adams,

cues.zh: 情境来自《银河系漫游指南》。
cues.en: and the situation is from "The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy."
And the situation it describes

cues.zh: 书中的主角——一个20世纪的人——
cues.en: is the hero of the book -- he's a 20th-century man --

cues.zh: 发现自己独自在一个陌生的星球上，
cues.en: finds himself alone on a strange planet

cues.zh: 那里只住着技术原始的民族。
cues.en: populated only by a technologically primitive people.
And he kind of assumes that, yes,
he'll become -- these villagers --
he'll become their emperor
and transform their society

cues.zh: 科学和元素的出色掌控
cues.en: with his wonderful command of technology
and science and the elements,
but, of course, realizes

cues.zh: 没有人类社会的其余部分，
cues.en: that without the rest of human society,

cues.zh: 他连三明治都几乎做不出来，
cues.en: he can barely make a sandwich,
let alone a toaster.
But he didn't have Wikipedia.
So I thought, okay,

cues.zh: 我要试着从零开始做一台电动烤面包机。
cues.en: I'll try and make an electric toaster from scratch.
And, working on the idea

cues.zh: 那就是最便宜的电动烤面包机
cues.en: that the cheapest electric toaster

cues.zh: 也应该是最容易逆向工程的，
cues.en: would also be the simplest to reverse-engineer,

cues.zh: 我去买了能找到的最便宜的烤面包机，
cues.en: I went and bought the cheapest toaster I could find,
took it home
and was kind of dismayed to discover
that, inside this object,
which I'd bought for just 3.49 pounds,
there were 400 different bits

cues.zh: 由一百多种不同的材料制成。
cues.en: made out of a hundred-plus different materials.

cues.zh: 我没有余生来做这个项目。
cues.en: I didn't have the rest of my life to do this project.
I had maybe nine months.

cues.zh: 所以我想，好吧，我从五种开始。
cues.en: So I thought, okay, I'll start with five.
And these were steel, mica,
plastic, copper and nickel.

cues.zh: 那么，从钢开始：你怎么制造钢？
cues.en: So, starting with steel: how do you make steel?
I went and knocked on the door

cues.zh: 找到了皇家矿业学院的
cues.en: of the Rio Tinto Chair

cues.zh: 力拓高级矿物提取教席教授
cues.en: of Advanced Mineral Extraction at the Royal School of Mines
and said, "How do you make steel?"
And Professor Cilliers was very kind

cues.zh: 给我详细讲解了这件事。
cues.en: and talked me through it.

cues.zh: 我在GCSE科学课上的模糊记忆是——
cues.en: And my vague rememberings from GCSE science --
well, steel comes from iron,

cues.zh: 所以我打电话给一家铁矿。
cues.en: so I phoned up an iron mine.

cues.zh: 我说：“嗨，我想做一个烤面包机。
cues.en: And said, "Hi, I'm trying to make a toaster.
Can I come up and get some iron?"

cues.zh: 不幸的是，我到那儿时——Ray出现了。
cues.en: Unfortunately, when I got there -- emerges Ray.
He had misheard me

cues.zh: 以为我来是因为我想做一张海报，
cues.en: and thought I was coming up because I was trying to make a poster,
and so wasn't prepared to take me into the mines.

cues.zh: 但经过一番软磨硬泡，我说服他带我去了。
cues.en: But after some nagging, I got him to do that.
(Video) Ray: It was Crease Limestone,
and that was produced
by sea creatures
350 million years ago
in a nice, warm,

cues.zh: 阳光充足的环境中形成的。
cues.en: sunny atmosphere.
When you study geology,

cues.zh: 你能看到过去发生了什么，
cues.en: you can see what's happened in the past,

cues.zh: 地球经历了巨大的变化。
cues.en: and there were terrific changes in the earth.

cues.zh: Thomas Thwaites：如你所见，他们挂起了圣诞装饰。
cues.en: Thomas Thwaites: As you can see, they had the Christmas decorations up.

cues.zh: 当然，它实际上已经不再是一个运作中的矿场了，
cues.en: And of course, it wasn't actually a working mine anymore,

cues.zh: 因为，尽管Ray曾在那里当矿工，
cues.en: because, though Ray was a miner there,
the mine had closed

cues.zh: 并被重新开放成了一个旅游景点，
cues.en: and had been reopened as a kind of tourist attraction,

cues.zh: 因为，当然，它在运营规模上无法竞争
cues.en: because, of course, it can't compete

cues.zh: 与正在进行的那些大规模作业相比
cues.en: on the scale of operations which are happening

cues.zh: 在南美、澳大利亚或其他地方。
cues.en: in South America, Australia, wherever.

cues.zh: 但不管怎样，我拿到了我那箱铁矿石
cues.en: But anyway, I got my suitcase of iron ore

cues.zh: 并乘火车把它拖回了伦敦，
cues.en: and dragged it back to London on the train,
and then was faced with the problem:

cues.zh: 好吧，你如何把这块岩石
cues.en: Okay, how do you make this rock
into components for a toaster?
So I went back to Professor Cilliers,
and he said, "Go to the library."
So I did

cues.zh: 并翻阅了冶金学的本科教科书——
cues.en: and was looking through the undergraduate textbooks on metallurgy --

cues.zh: 对于我想要做的事情完全没用。
cues.en: completely useless for what I was trying to do.

cues.zh: 因为他们当然不会告诉你具体怎么做
cues.en: Because, of course, they don't actually tell you how to do it

cues.zh: 如果你想自己动手，又没有冶炼厂的话。
cues.en: if you want to do it yourself and you don't have a smelting plant.

cues.zh: 所以我最后去了科学史图书馆
cues.en: So I ended up going to the History of Science Library
and looking at this book.
This is the first textbook on metallurgy
written in the West, at least.

cues.zh: 你可以看到那幅木版画
cues.en: And there you can see that woodcut

cues.zh: 基本上就是我最后做的事。
cues.en: is basically what I ended up doing.

cues.zh: 只不过我用的是吹叶机，而不是风箱。
cues.en: But instead of a bellows, I had a leaf blower.
(Laughter)

cues.zh: 而这件事在整个项目中反复出现，
cues.en: And that was something that reoccurred throughout the project,

cues.zh: 那就是，你想做的尺度越小，
cues.en: was, the smaller the scale you want to work on,

cues.zh: 你就得回溯到越久远的时代。
cues.en: the further back in time you have to go.
And so this is after
a day and about half a night
smelting this iron.
I dragged out this stuff,
and it wasn't iron.
But luckily,

cues.zh: 我在网上找到了一项专利
cues.en: I found a patent online

cues.zh: 是关于用微波的工业炉，
cues.en: for industrial furnaces that use microwaves,
and at 30 minutes at full power,

cues.zh: 我就把整个过程完成了。
cues.en: and I was able to finish off the process.
So, my next --
(Applause)
The next thing I was trying to get was copper.
Again, this mine

cues.zh: 它曾是世界上最大的铜矿。
cues.en: was once the largest copper mine in the world.
It's not anymore,

cues.zh: 但我找到了一位退休的地质学教授
cues.en: but I found a retired geology professor
to take me down,

cues.zh: 他说：“好吧，我让你取一些矿里的水。”
cues.en: and he said, "Okay, I'll let you have some water from the mine."

cues.zh: 我之所以对取水感兴趣
cues.en: And the reason I was interested in getting water
is because water which goes through mines
becomes kind of acidic
and will start picking up,
dissolving the minerals from the mine.

cues.zh: 一个很好的例子是力拓河，
cues.en: And a good example of this is the Rio Tinto,
which is in Portugal.

cues.zh: 如你所见，里面溶解了大量的矿物质。
cues.en: As you can see, it's got lots and lots of minerals dissolved in it.
So many such

cues.zh: 现在它只是细菌的家园
cues.en: that it's now just a home for bacteria

cues.zh: 这些细菌非常喜欢酸性、有毒的环境。
cues.en: who really like acidic, toxic conditions.

cues.zh: 但不管怎样，我拖回来的水
cues.en: But anyway, the water I dragged back

cues.zh: 来自安格尔西岛，也就是矿所在的地方——
cues.en: from the Isle of Anglesey where the mine was --
there was enough copper in it
such that I could cast the pins

cues.zh: 我的金属电插头的插脚。
cues.en: of my metal electric plug.
So my next thing: I was off to Scotland
to get mica.
And mica is a mineral
which is a very good insulator
and very good at insulating electricity.
That's me getting mica.

cues.zh: 今天我要讲的最后一种材料是塑料，
cues.en: And the last material I'm going to talk about today is plastic,
and, of course,

cues.zh: 我的烤面包机必须有一个塑料外壳。
cues.en: my toaster had to have a plastic case.

cues.zh: 塑料是廉价电子产品的
cues.en: Plastic is the defining feature
of cheap electrical goods.

cues.zh: 塑料来自石油，所以我打电话给BP，
cues.en: And so plastic comes from oil, so I phoned up BP
and spent a good half an hour

cues.zh: 试图说服BP的公关办公室，
cues.en: trying to convince the PR office at BP

cues.zh: 如果他们能把我送到石油钻井平台上，
cues.en: that it would be fantastic for them
if they flew me to an oil rig

cues.zh: 那对他们来说会是件大好事。
cues.en: and let me have a jug of oil.

cues.zh: BP现在显然有更多的事情要操心。
cues.en: BP obviously has a bit more on their mind now.
But even then
they weren't convinced

cues.zh: 只说：“好吧，我们会给你回电话”——结果一直没回。
cues.en: and said, "Okay, we'll phone you back" -- never did.

cues.zh: 于是我去寻找其他制造塑料的方法。
cues.en: So I looked at other ways of making plastic.
And you can actually make plastic

cues.zh: 从植物提取的油，当然也可以从淀粉来制造。
cues.en: from obviously oils which come from plants, but also from starches.
So this is attempting to make
potato starch plastic.

cues.zh: 有一阵子看起来效果很不错。
cues.en: And for a while that was looking really good.

cues.zh: 我把它倒进模具里，你们可以看到，
cues.en: I poured it into the mold, which you can see there,

cues.zh: 这个模具是我用树干做的。
cues.en: which I've made from a tree trunk.

cues.zh: 有一阵子看起来挺好的，
cues.en: And it was looking good for a while,

cues.zh: 但我把它放在外面，因为得放在外面晾干，
cues.en: but I left it outside, because you had to leave it outside to dry,
and unfortunately I came back

cues.zh: 发现蜗牛在吃土豆里未水解的部分。
cues.en: and there were snails eating the unhydrolyzed bits of potato.

cues.zh: 所以有点走投无路之下，
cues.en: So kind of out of desperation,
I decided that I could think laterally.

cues.zh: 地质学家其实已经命名了——
cues.en: And geologists have actually christened --

cues.zh: 嗯，他们在争论要不要命名——
cues.en: well, they're debating whether to christen --
the age that we're living in --

cues.zh: 他们在争论要不要把它定为一个新的地质世
cues.en: they're debating whether to make it a new geological epoch
called the Anthropocene, the age of Man.
And that's because geologists of the future

cues.zh: 会看到一种急剧的变化
cues.en: would kind of see a sharp shift

cues.zh: 就在如今正在沉积的岩层里。
cues.en: in the strata of rock that is being laid down now.

cues.zh: 突然间，它会变得有放射性，来自切尔诺贝利
cues.en: So suddenly, it will become kind of radioactive from Chernobyl
and the 2,000 or so nuclear bombs
that have been set off since 1945.

cues.zh: 而且还会有一个灭绝事件——
cues.en: And there'd also be an extinction event --
like fossils would suddenly disappear.
And also, I thought
that there would be
synthetic polymers,
plastics, embedded in the rock.

cues.zh: 于是我查找了一种塑料——
cues.en: So I looked up a plastic --

cues.zh: 所以我决定，我可以开采
cues.en: so I decided that I could mine
some of this modern-day rock.
And I went up to Manchester

cues.zh: 参观一个叫Axion Recycling的地方。
cues.en: to visit a place called Axion Recycling.

cues.zh: 他们处在所谓WEEE的最前沿，
cues.en: And they're at the sharp end of what's called the WEEE,

cues.zh: 也就是欧洲的电子电气废弃物指令。
cues.en: which is this European electrical and electronic waste directive.
And that was brought into force

cues.zh: 试图应对那堆积如山的東西
cues.en: to try and deal with the mountain of stuff

cues.zh: 那些东西刚被制造出来
cues.en: that is just being made
and then living for a while in our homes
and then going to landfill.
But this is it.
(Music)
(Laughter)
So there's a picture
of my toaster.
(Applause)
That's it without the case on.

cues.zh: 这就是它放在架子上的样子。
cues.en: And there it is on the shelves.
Thanks.
(Applause)

cues.zh: Bruno Giussani：我听说你确实插过一次电。
cues.en: Bruno Giussani: I'm told you did plug it in once.
TT: Yeah, I did plug it in.

cues.zh: 我不知道你们能不能看到，
cues.en: I don't know if you could see,

cues.zh: 但我一直没能给电线做绝缘。
cues.en: but I was never able to make insulation for the wires.
Kew Gardens were insistent

cues.zh: 不让我去割他们的橡胶树。
cues.en: that I couldn't come and hack into their rubber tree.

cues.zh: 所以电线是没有绝缘的。
cues.en: So the wires were uninsulated.
So there was 240 volts
going through these homemade copper wires,
homemade plug.
And for about five seconds,

cues.zh: 烤面包机真的烤了面包，
cues.en: the toaster toasted,
but then, unfortunately,

cues.zh: 加热元件有点把自己熔化了。
cues.en: the element kind of melted itself.

cues.zh: 但说实话，我觉得这算是部分成功。
cues.en: But I considered it a partial success, to be honest.
BG: Thomas Thwaites. TT: Thanks.
